title: Mastering Choroidal Melanoma: From Diagnosis to Definitive Management
summary: Choroidal melanoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, requiring a multidisciplinary approach for globe preservation and systemic survival. This guide covers the gold-standard COMS-based treatment protocols and diagnostic pathways.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Choroidal melanoma arises from uveal melanocytes. Incidence: 5-7 per million per year in Caucasians. Peak incidence occurs in the 6th decade of life. Major risk factors include light iris color, fair skin, inability to tan, and presence of ocular/oculodermal melanocytosis.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup (The 'To Find Small Ocular Melanoma' Criteria)
content: T: Thickness >2mm
F: Fluid (Subretinal)
S: Symptoms (Photopsia/Blur)
O: Orange pigment (Lipofuscin)
M: Margin (Disc proximity)
U: Ultrasonographic hollowness
H: Halo (Absence of)

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect Malignancy
content: Presence of subretinal fluid (not associated with other pathologies)
Documentation of growth on serial exam
Orange pigment on tumor surface
Acoustic hollowness on B-scan ultrasonography
Tumor thickness exceeding 2mm

sections.title: Treatment Modalities (COMS Protocols)
content: Step 1: Plaque Brachytherapy (I-125, Ru-106, Pd-103) - Gold standard for medium-sized tumors.
Step 2: Proton Beam Irradiation - Indicated for large tumors or juxtapapillary locations.
Step 3: Transpupillary Thermotherapy (TTT) - Adjunctive therapy for thin tumors.
Step 4: Enucleation - Indicated for massive tumors with no visual potential or significant extraocular extension.
Step 5: Anti-VEGF therapy - Used post-radiation to manage radiation maculopathy/retinopathy.

content.explanation: To Find Small Ocular Melanoma: Thickness, Fluid, Symptoms, Orange pigment, Margin, Ultra-sound, Halo absence.

sections.title: Recent Advances: Genetic Prognostication
content: Gene Expression Profiling (GEP): Class 1A/1B (low risk), Class 2 (high metastatic risk).
Chromosome 3 Monosomy: Strong correlation with metastatic disease.
BAP1 mutation: Frequently associated with Class 2 tumors and poor systemic prognosis.
Liquid Biopsy: Investigational use of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in aqueous humor.
